item.title: Weeknotes No.88
item.description:
I am sure you’ve noticed, waiting patiently for my weeknotes, that this is turning into more of a monthly notes; there is a reason for this - in fact, more than one, but work-wise reason, I am on one of those projects that I can’t really discuss openly - you know the type, needs a certain security level.
I shall share as much as I can, but without oversharing!

Challenge accepted


It’s been busy, work is super busy right now - I am the sole designer on the project, so this means I run the User research sessions, I also write up the findings, I am, of course, the designer and the dot-joiner-upper. This will then lead to fortnightly presentations from me to the wider team (100-200 ppl), often in separate meetings and differing needs and presentation requirements. AND you know what? I bloody love it, throw me into a project with a lot to do - and I couldn’t be happy, something about a pig in something, but the rest of the saying escapes me.

I have been using Figma almost exclusively for the last 5 months, inventing the producut’s Design System (leaning into Tremor UI as a framework), as well as organising MVP deliverables and Post MVP deliverables, all led from the above mentioned UR sessions, which is powering a backlog and almost fueling my early assumptions (but.. I am 15-20 years in this game now!).

Very hands-on, as you can see, as well as leadership, it’s married really well on this project, and I know from the work I’ve delivered (and how I’ve delivered), I’ve been handed the trust and got that seat all designers crave.

Updating my own portfolio


Like a pig in whatever, I’ve also been updating my own portfolio - designing it out in Figma, writing case studies again and updating all sorts (CVs, LinkedIn, etc.).

What led to this madness, you ask? My connections/messages have been very mid-level led (if not lower). Upon talking to recruiters (I have a list of trusted and faithful ones!) they let me know very quickly that I can easily do the work (and have done with their references), but maybe I’m worth a little bit more, I can certainly do in the weeds and, I am also adapt in the bid/stakeholder/lets make this work chats.

Speaking to my mentor(s), it became VERY apparent how I am showcasing work done is very senior level, it follows a very strict pattern of:
Here’s a screen grab of my prototype. Here is what I did on the prototype, but no mention of what else, and it’s the what else which makes me come to work, gets my engine ticking over.
I am yet to work on a project in the last 10 years where I can “just do design” and to be honest - I am unsure I would ever take on a project that is like that, but I am also influencing, mentoring, giving back and dare-I-say arguing for the power of design.. and then i’ll do a prototype at the end.
So keep an eye out for that, it’s well overdue but also one of those “oooh gosh, now I see it” moments!

On leave and cold


We did a little glamping getaway at Ty Llewelyn Glamping and Camping, which was so much fun. We visited the bro-in-law and survived Storm Dave, which was a bloody experience in a tent!
Turns out Wales has a lot of roads in the middle of nowhere - driving through fields of cows, to no roads at all, but its defo a road on the map. A street light wouldn’t go amiss either!

It was great, though, and I’d always recommend it, but I fancy a hotel/ Airbnb stay next time… those pesky cold showers are a little rough in the morning.

A playlist for March


Being heavily inspired by a pal of mine (Chrish), who, as far as I can remember, has done a playlist for every month, and I loved that idea… and finally got around to doing it myself! So here are my March ‘26 tunes that struck a chord, some are new, some are songs I’ve just heard but have been out for a while, or some are just bangers that have kept me going. It’s a collection of whatever-no-rules.

Roll on next week! ✌️

item.title: Weeknotes No.87
item.description:
Half term is over, which means I can do things without being asked to play Lego City on the Switch, which I absolutely love gaming with my kids, but not all the time (scratch that… I love playing games all the time). Oh, and the requests for snacks.. I am unsure what’s robbing my creative juices more - getting fruit and veg into the kids or my day job, my 2 little ones are the most demanding stakeholders I’ve ever worked with - HR would have a fieldday with them!

Contract update!


I am at that weird part of my contract, will it be renewed, or has my time come to an end? Either way, it’s been amazing. The work we are doing is proper stuff, it’ll go live, AND it’s wanted by its users, who have been a dream to work alongside. They know what they want, have communicated it clearly, but the fun is also in the parts where it hasn’t been clear. Give a designer a puzzle and watch them get their thinking face and hat on. I love this stuff!

I am doing things in this project I havent done in a long while, working on a design system that has very different components for very different reasons - things can range from table data - very run of the mill show data off, to insuring as much squeezes on the page as possible without the overwhelming the user issue, enlarging lines of text shown in tables (but the funactionality again, not taking up space) to my latest crush - designing visualisations for data! I’m still on my presentation road trip as well, it’s really good to be presenting work to very senior stakeholders (and being commended on my passion for this) whilst working in the weeds, this feels right for me at the moment, and I am very much enjoying doing the design leadership and design doing.

AI, it’s uses, it’s useless, it’s taking over the world.. or is it?


We spoke on Thursday (breaking the fourth wall here!) on the Podcast 1 Pixel Out about AI and its effects on jobs, our day to day and life - it was so interesting to see other people’s experiences and what the future feels like it could be. Can’t wait for it to come out and see what people think. The topic is wide-ranging, and we touched the surface, but it came across as 4 designers (who all do very different jobs within design) discussing issues, positives, and worries. It’s, as usual, a very open and flowing conversation with challenging questions - it’s one of those “down the pub with mates” chats that is being recorded. I also dropped in one of two mentions of bobbin and Bumble (think it might be 4-5) - free ads!

🎧 Listen & follow:
→ Spotify
→ Amazon
→ Apple

Let me know what you think, but roll on next week! ✌️

item.title: Weeknotes No.86
item.description:
This week started with a bang!


Well, it started with shit weather and a leaky patio door, which is obviously a pain in the bum and a job on our to-do list. And by ‘fix,’ I mean completely demolish the back of the house and reconfigure how the house works. CAN’T WAIT FOR THE DUST!

But let’s not jump ahead of ourselves and get wet feet, last week was great. I spent a day working at Stocked in Horsforth in a co-working space alongside Emma’s Mastered class host, the ever brilliant Sophie, and it was just great to chat to creative folk working in a space that isn’t familiar to me - I heard chats around coaching, marketing, design, content writing and bagels!
I will certainly do co-working again, and the host of Stocked was wonderful - incredibly friendly and just a joy (and the attached shop is 1000% going to have my money soon!)

More recently,


I’ve been on the offensive, presenting the work to all who wish to hear and see what we’ve been doing as a team. It’s often a thing I push my team to do, instead of “pull” we also “push” communication back - invite the audience into our world and share what we’ve been doing and why.

My presentations tend to be quite structured and land (usually!), it looks something like:

  • Shape why you are here and what to expect from this presentation
    This sets the scene and checks that they even want to be here

  • This design is MVP AND a very relaxed presentation, nudge me if you want to ask a question, anytime, and I'll happily stop
    This lets everyone, we all own this, not just the designer and developers

  • User needs AND business needs, what are they, what did they say
    I show quotes, always with the quotes - it puts "real" to it!

  • Summarise the problems, what are we going to tackle (it's not everything)
    Set the scene for the next stage of the presentation..

  • Show the visuals, walk through journeys
    I use the 'jobs to be done' model to present this: no solo screens, but a reason why the user is doing a thing - usually from from login to submit. This helps the user 'feel in the design' - thanks to David Evans for that nudge!

  • Provide space for questions, it's a simple one, but I've seen so many presentations run the full 30 minutes or so, I always plan 10 minutes at least for next steps, and Q and A.

All the presentations have landed, they’ve ranged from the actual end users to very senior stakeholders - I often call these meetings “keeping the lights on”, and I think I’ve managed to get a new candle to the lanteen!

What’s happening elsewhere


Bobbin and Bumble is getting a facelift, and I’m dusting down my code chops once again, which is fun. Never did I think I’d be coding in Liquid again like the old days, but here we are (I’m building my design, it’s like the 2000s all over again!). The wave is real over there, and I love seeing Emma grow, appear on podcasts, and share her brilliant story.

Speaking of podcasts..


This week I was under the spotlight, which means.. the conversation was all about Contracting. It was fun being cornered by my two favourite designers (aside from you); listen to it and let me know how many times I swear (i reckon I didn’t hit double figures…).

🎧 Listen & follow:
→ Spotify
→ Amazon
→ Apple podcasts

Next week


I am unsure I can think straight - I’m currently writing this, watching my daughter swim, and it’s about 105 degrees, and I am starting to think it’s a great idea to jump off the diving board. Due to recent events, I tend to not plan - life’s been so unexpected at the moment that things change and take my emotions with it, but I do have a family birthday party to attend, Robyn is getting graded at swimming (which I hope she does well ‘cos shes brilliant) and I wonder how much pizza i’ll eat.

Thanks for reading. Catch you in the next one. ✌️

item.title: Weeknotes No.85
item.description:
I’m back!


It’s been an age since I last wrote anything on LinkedIn or my website. I have struggled to find any motivation to do anything over the past month or two. My personal life took a hit, and I just found life overwhelming, but as with everything, the sun keeps shining, the earth keeps going round, and I refocused myself and, I guess, took stock of where I am, who I am and why I am, which was incredibly insightful. I am not out of the woods, but the sun feels warmer and food tastes nicer.

Work-wise, I’ve moved teams and am now in the deep end of Universal Credits. It’s lovely to be back and help make welfare smoother and cleaner. I am still over multiple teams - but it’s manageable and doable.

In fact…


I wrote the previous sentence at the end of the week (25th September), and I am writing this next part on 30th September. I have moved on from DWP and am returning to HMRC to work on a one-Mikey-band project alongside a team of developers. Of course, I can’t share anything more (mostly because I’m not 100%!), but I am looking forward to a new challenge, and pushing myself harder and further into data-led and experience-led design. It’s amazing how life throws hurdles, challenges, and opportunities.

I recently decided to stop gaming (as much as I do in the evenings) and read, and bought “It’s not how good you are, it’s how good you want to be” by Paul Arden. Every section is an absolute zinger, I can’t put it down but I need to digest what I’ve just read.
With Emma, she says stop, and we pick a page and read it out loud - it’s been amazing to then follow it up with a story about ourselves to compare where it sits in our career/life. It’s been an incredible coffee/tea chat, something I’ve missed working from home.

Some random updates - but it’s more of a warning, ALWAYS check when your phone contract ends, and your TV/broadband package. I ignored all the emails and warnings and found out my deal wasn’t a deal; both needed to be binned months ago, and it’s shocking how late I looked into this. For example, almost the same deal with Three has chopped off £245.28 per year, which is madness! Also, leaving Sky and going to Virgin for my TV/Broadband means I shall save a whopping £576.12, so in the space of 60 minutes I’ve managed to get a better deal (more channels, EU roaming) and save £821.40! That is either pension money or kids’ savings!

Watch us wreck the mic, watch us wreck the mic, watch us wreck the mic… Psyche


And finally, but not lastly - I kicked off a busy time in my life with a podcast with a fabulous bunch of friends that I am forever in awe of and would ideally listen to them talk (which works well as it’s a podcast!), which I shall be speaking about a lot more in future weeknotes, called 1PixelOut

🎧 Listen & follow:
→ On Spotify
→ On Apple
→ On Amazon

We all have various experiences, in life and work and talk about them openly whilst sharing George Clooney facts (IYKYK).

Thanks for reading. Catch you in the next one. ✌️

item.title: Weeknotes No.84
item.description:
Hay fever


Let’s just cut to the chase: hay fever can F-OFF!

It’s been a blast in the sun, swimming pools are out, BBQs are on the go, and I forgot to put suncream on and got burnt - but what’s a quick summer without a red face?

Re-brand, usual drama


GOV.UK’s new branding caught the eye of many people, loads concentrating on “the dot”, which is a shame, usually as most re-brands go - it’s natural for people to discuss the cost, the work etc, but there is more to come “under the hood” and I do think it’s a pretty good re-brand.

The point, among many, is to be more modern, attract a younger audience to apps, services and become (I would imagine) more self-serving, similar to a project I worked on for NHS (absolute shameless plug) - people are, I believe, being led to owning their data more which I hope leads to better-designed services that are easier to use and less overwhelming.

Work-wise


I kick-started a prioritise work meeting to discuss what is next, what is left, and what I need to work through quicker than others - I love these meetings, and it’s great to ensure everyone is in the loop of my workload and their workload and if I can help anyone out in the team. This led to us finding work that was hidden away and needed to be done - which I’m more than happy to help out; this also included a “bucket” of Accessibility issues that were found during testing - this is my bread and butter, so delighted to fix/advise before launch!

I offered to support (and was accepted) the lead designer in my portfolio area (this means a group of teams in a collective) - there is a lot of work knocking around, and much of it isnt pushing pixels around, and whilst I am here, I always tell people to lean on me, I’ve been through a lot, managed a lot and got all the scars to prove it, also known as “send me in where you wouldn’t send a perm” - that’s the point, right?

Life, f’ing Etsy and KANBANNNNNNN


Jasper’s induction day at school; this blows my brain working out he’s not-so-little-anymore; I mean, he’s little, but not AS little anymore. Hold up, if he’s getting older, does that mean I am?

Bobbin and Bumble’s Etsy shop being the forever piece of shi..work i’m on - I found a helpful resource on YouTube with a different tact, so I am trying a new strategy, and this is the last thing i’ll speak on this (excluding the odd post here and there) as it’s annoying me never those that read this about my dreadful Etsy adventures

Bobbin and Bumble are again in a new chapter. As a pretty senior designer and giving more and more of my evenings and weekends to run the ever-growing business, we discussed how we manage workload to avoid duplication and ensure alignment, and, let’s say, it together - KANBAN.

We have gone for Trello. It’s easy, and this helps explain to Emma how we run the board. But the biggest worry I have is the overwhelming issue of the ever-growing backlog. Of course, I understand how it works, but I can imagine if you are used to just doing work, seeing it written down in smaller chunks (2-week rule) might be very disheartening, but it’ll be a good thing in the end when it works well.

Thanks for reading. Catch you in the next one. ✌️

item.title: Weeknotes No.83
item.description:
Contracting life


To kick off the week, early on, there was a discussion around the future of contracting within my department, which was handled brilliantly by the Lead and reminded me of the ups and downs of leadership (something I miss more and more as my time in contracting goes on).

This will eventually lead to the “green sash” on LinkedIn, but I am unsure about the short term—I am contracted until January 2026. I also realise this is the lifestyle we choose as contracting and completely understand, something I often tell those who seem to lust after contracting—you must be comfortable putting yourself out there and also be vulnerable to plans changing upon a throw of a dice.

Schools out for.. summer or it’s about to start


Jasper (my 4-year-old mini-twin and boss) starts his school adventure soon, so it’s been a week of understanding and meeting his future teachers—emotions are high in this house. We’ve done this once before, and it doesn’t get easier! But he’s excited, and so are we—but the puzzle of how the hell we do school pick up and drop off with one car is the impossible task.

Best talk about the work!


Workwise, it really feels like I am wrapping up on this project now. Talks are ongoing about placing me elsewhere, and I’m really happy to return to my old stomping ground in the welfare department. It’s moved on a great ton, and it feels wild that many years ago, the team I was in made such a huge impact that I can see it daily. Loads of meetings, loads of planning workloads for the big launch and as an added bonus, I would say im a professional now at using Lucid, Mural seems a lifetime away.

It’s pretty obvious now, but I spend many evenings working on Bobbin and Bumble, and my recent efforts have been working within Etsy. I disucssed this last week, but it’s a platform that was head and shoulders above so many others, but more recently, it feels like it’s lost its way; it feels more centred less on shop owners and ALL on buyers - yes, it’s a catch 22 situation, but as a seller, i have very little idea on how to improve the shop, how to optimise listings and what I am doing. It often changes with multiple rumours and their guides that are outdated or contradicting. Platforms come and go, and I think we’re slowly getting to the point where we let this one go. I am unsure of its value, point in the market, and where it is heading.

I have started looking into case studies again; I am so far behind on them it’s unreal - I have work at NHS that I have presented but never put down in writing, I have my recent DEFRA work as well, again - spoken about but never written and maybe my AI work at AstraZeneca too… and my current piece of work is most certainly case study worthy too!

This is a short and sweet update from me; let me know how your week was.

Thanks for reading. Catch you in the next one. ✌️

item.title: Weeknotes No.82
item.description:
It’s a fresh new week, full of hopes and dreams — which reminded me of a brilliant BBC documentary from 1984. A while back eh.

1984: Bandersnatch, Bailiffs and the Battle for a Hit Game is well worth a watch if you’re into retro gaming like I am. Full of ambition, chaos, bailiffs — the lot. The giants of that era had huge dreams. Too big? Maybe. It’s great telly, though.

Father’s Day = Doing Nothing


We celebrated Father’s Day best — by doing nothing after a hectic Saturday. And it was glorious. No jobs, no rushing, no nothing. Just leaning back in the garden, messing about on the Switch 2, and wondering what game to play next.

No one in the house complained of being bored either, so it feels like a very much overdue rest.

🏅 Big Saturday for the Small One


Saturday was a great day all round. My daughter had a synchronised swimming competition and finished 9th out of 116. Incredible. She’s won comps before, but this was a harder one - and she held her own.

She’s in the pool around 14 hours a week (!), and she goes to every single lesson. This is all on her, and it’s inspiring and not something I did when I was 9. She’s brilliant.

Evenings = Switch + Shopify


Evenings were spent switching between two things:

  • Completing Gunslinger on the Switch 2 (solid little game)
  • Chipping away at Bobbin and Bumble tasks and to-dos

Productive and relaxing, which is a rare combo.

Good Read – Design in 2025


I’m a big fan of Tom and his writing. His recent post on product design hiring in 2025 gave me a bit of a case-study-kick-up-the-arse. You know the drill, I am 2-3 years behind and needed it.

It’s also no surprise that the most desirable designers are all-rounders—I’ve seen that when hiring and being hired. The rise of the super IC feels very real.

There are loads of Lead-level designers knocking about at the moment, it makes me wonder if expectations around what a Lead is have shifted. (Tom’s first point made me pause and think this)

Anyway, it’s worth a read, especially if you’re a designer thinking about your next move. Let me know what you think (and Tom, too). It’s an exciting (and slightly scary) time to be in the field.

Work & Crit Wins


This week was filled with many discussions with developers, mostly around whether we could simplify or reduce design work to meet delivery deadlines.

I like those challenges. I genuinely believe in “less is best”, especially when we don’t have strong evidence a thing was even wanted. When you weigh effort vs value, a lot of work just isn’t worth dying on any hill.

I’d rather ship something meaningful than waste time polishing a feature that maybe isnt needed as much as we think. If people do care, they’ll let us know — and we’ll iterate.

But it wasn’t all “What can we cut?” chat. We had a cracking design crit session where minds stretched, devs felt heard, we found a smart way through a tricky problem, and even squeezed in a “let’s do more of this” moment.

What’s Next?


This weekend: BBQ with good friends and (hopefully) no rain.

Also — do I know anyone who runs a shop on Etsy? If so, nudge me! 👋

Thanks for reading. Catch you in the next one. ✌️

item.title: Weeknotes No.81
item.description:
🎤 A Bit of Everything This Week…

A weekend away in Liverpool “with the lads,” dusting off my HTML prototype skills (forgot how much I love it), navigating some tax code madness, and chatting non-stop design for a future “thing” 🎤.

There’s been loads going on this week — combined with previous thoughts I shared about being more present as a coach and on LinkedIn. I’ve started that adventure again, and turns out: impressions on both LinkedIn and the blog post for last week’s Weeknotes went through the roof. A bit of vanity, sure, but it feels good. I won’t be checking the numbers again though — I know working inside a business that social media likes, do not equal sales!

🙌 Designer Shoutout


I also want to shout out a designer I’m currently supporting on his journey to his next role. We haven’t quite cracked it yet - but he’s so close.

If you’re looking for a product or interaction designer, or know a great place we can submit his CV, let me know!.

💔 Sky Bet / Flutter Redundancies


Plenty of things have caught my eye this week. The big one saw a lot of ex-colleagues being made redundant at Sky Bet/Flutter.
It’s a challenging read seeing this. Those that had the news - I have no doubt - will find themselves in employment quickly, as that company only hires golden eggs.

Is this another sign that the Leeds Digital Community is potentially fading compared to what it once was? I hope not.

🏢 Remote Working vs. Office (Again)


Another was the discussion around remote working against coming into the office - this will never leave us - and one I touched on during a recent podcast I appeared in somewhere (wait and see!).

I won’t discuss my full opinion, but needless to say, I believe it’s incredibly short-sighted to think a request to go back into an office will suddenly improve output at the cost of many things. It lowers access for people (parents, those with accessibility requirements etc). In the last 3 years, I’ve never worked with “my team” in the same county - nevermind in the same office!

🧩 Restructure at Work


This week, work is having a restructure - another one, yes - but they all feel right. They feel like they make sense and, in the future, feel like a big brave move in the interest of users (and not a cost-cutting exercise).

I love working at the DWP; the community and group of designers feel like a place to work. They are incredibly supportive, fun to work with, and very clever.

They’ve just posted a job for a Lead Interaction Designer - I highly recommend applying:
🔗 View the role on LinkedIn

🧪 National Rollout Prototype Progress


I’m still working on the final prototype for a national rollout - a project that will support millions of claimants and hundreds of work coaches.

It’s not easy. I’m in more than one team, and a lot has changed since I last picked it up - from little tweaks to full flow changes. But this isn’t just a “testing prototype” anymore. It’s become:

  • A training platform for Ops
  • A source of truth for documentation
  • A way to promote the service, inform future investment, and show “how to do it”

I always aim to leave the team with a clear, archived “here’s what we delivered” flow - so future teams can understand why and how we did it, without relying on a fragile live prototype (which is currently a nightmare to update due to security blocks!).

🛍️ Bobbin and Bumble Updates


On the Bobbin and Bumble side, I’m making updates as I go - particularly the navigation and core content.

Taking a proper break (without my MacBook!) was the best thing I could’ve done. I switched off completely and came back with a fresh perspective.

The site needs a refresh, yes. But more than that:

  • It needs UX thinking
  • It needs a rethink of the information architecture
  • It needs better content across all pages

It’s e-commerce (or commerce depending on how you view shops), and the end game is to improve conversions continually.

💬 Chats with Ex-Directs


I caught up with a couple of ex-colleagues this week - people I used to line-manage and it was honestly just brilliant to talk.

Not about portfolios.
Not about “what job are you after?”

But about where they are now, as people.

They’re reflecting more on what makes them happy and less on the ladder. I’m here for that. They’ll absolutely smash their next steps.

And if you’re in a similar space and fancy a nudge, I’m always happy to chat - just drop me a message.

🎮 Nintendo Switch 2 is a Hit


Final update — I bought a Nintendo Switch 2, and in short — it’s bloody brilliant.

It was so good that I cancelled my Xbox Game Pass, which I used often for the wind-down. To have such a console on the move is incredible; it feels nice, and the games (if you look around) are not expensive. I haven’t gone for any Switch 2 games yet, but Cyberpunk, I am watching you.

🎧 Listen of the Week


I Prevail is a band I’ve loved for years. They’ve released a new song — gone are the melodies of the other singer (Brian). They’ve gone into their heavy period, which is interesting (I love both styles), but this is heavy!
🎵 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lCM2YxDg6OQ

Thanks for reading. Catch you in the next one. ✌️

item.title: Weeknotes No.80
item.description:
Morocco, Muses & Mural Transfers

During my birthday week and holiday, I decided it was time to be much more visible on LinkedIn.

Over the past month (maybe even longer), I’m not sure why I haven’t posted much. Sometimes weeknotes slipped into monthly notes. I stopped sharing friends’ posts, commenting on them, or even being interested in what was going on in the industry.

Could I be tired of it all?
Yes - you’re damn right I am.
But I feel experienced enough now to help steer an industry that feels quite lost.

It’s less about shouting into the void, and more about showing up with solutions. Less moaning, more making. Less “what’s wrong with this?”, and more “here’s what’s working”.

Shoutout to two good eggs:

  • Gavin Elliot, who’s showing real optimism around the role of AI in design.
  • Tom Scott, who’s still out here bringing knowledge to the masses.

So with that — you’ll see more of me. What I’m working on. What I’m thinking. Things I usually don’t talk about for whatever reason.

Yes, it’s one of those “I’m going to turn up more” posts…
But honestly? It’s overdue. And it’s going to help me grow, express myself better, and sharpen my communication skills.

✈️ Holiday Mode: Activated


Let’s switch gears: Morocco was fucking ace.

It helps massively when your wife is a professional holiday booker. No resorts — she plans tours of countries.
We went hotel to hotel across Morocco: jungle, desert, sea, mad mad cities. It’s a place more diverse than I ever imagined.

Best holiday of my life? That’s still Bali. But Morocco comes close.

🎥 Shameless plug: Go show some love to Robyn & Mimi’s travel Instagram — it’s full of dreamy reels from the trip.

🧠 Back to Work (Kinda)


I’ve returned to work, gone through all the emails, transferred my Mural boards to Lucid, arranged catch-up meetings, and… opened Jira.
Confluence? Still not emotionally ready. Give me time.

I’m likely leaving this team in the coming months. So before I go, I want to leave behind:

  • A solid archive of design flows
  • A prototype of the national rollout
  • A clear Confluence trail of where things are, why they are, and what we realistically aimed to deliver

I’m hoping to join another team. We’ll see.

🎧 Listen of the Week


Holiday listening was all about recalibrating my mind.
People like Jim Rohn, Les Brown, and Alan Watts helped me reconnect with parts of myself I might’ve left behind to prioritise work.

And musically, I discovered a band called Amistat.
Their song “Seasons” had that same vibe as Crosby, Stills, Nash & Young — and I’ve had them on repeat ever since.

Thanks for reading. Catch you in the next one. ✌️

item.title: Weeknotes No.79
item.description:
It has been a busy one. We launched our service, and this means we have to go to Sheffield for regular User Research sessions (often called User Testing, but I recall Ben Holliday once correcting everyone, saying WE ARE NOT TESTING THE USER - which I’ve carried with me for years).

It’s tiring work. During the school holidays, it’s not ideal that I leave the house early and return home late, but it’s also been beneficial to see the service in people’s hands in real life, working and working well!

I’ve enjoyed it - the work coach I’m sitting with is a complete superstar; he’s so good at his role; he is calm, helpful, and a real star player with the people approaching his desk. He is why people get jobs; he is why people feel confident to keep trying, keep applying, and keep going - because whatever silly newspapers or idiots say, it is not an easy job market right now. The claimants I’ve met are not what you expect if you believe the media (which I knew already); they want to work, they desperately want to provide their own income and they are doing everything and anything to land a role.

Going forward, we are pushing out more features and milestones, which will help the Work Coaches give better support to customers/claimants and, in turn, help turn those job seekers into job workers.
There have been twists and turns in this delivery cycle, but so much credit has to go to the Design and Development team. They and we have really supported the rollout, which at times has felt chaotic and heated. However, we landed it, and seeing it in the wild feels like some great decisions were made throughout the ideation and build of the service.

I am leading the team on the changes from the User Research, influencing from afar into making changes - the deadlines are tight, oh so tight - so I’m leaning on my experience on what will have the most significant whack for the smallest buck; this is where we are right now with time and costings. It’s a huge challenge, and I can hear those blog posts that write the perfect world screaming in my ears - but, if I’m honest, I’ve never had the perfect design process. I am here to deliver something great for the country AND its users; if we are agile - then the process has to shift, too.
